description:
FILED s484d (2026-09-14).  t/op/stat.t produced NO rows until this session
(#1590's `is_linux_container` was an undef-fn abort at its first call).  It now
produces all 111 of perl's rows, 94 passing -- **full row parity** -- and the
14 failures are the file's real content.  From
scratch/s484d/keep-cons/op_stat.t.out:

  rows 37, 38  `ls and -c agreeing on /dev (195 197)` / `-S (0 1)`: stat's
    st_rdev and st_blocks.  PCL answers 195 and 0 where the device says 197
    and 1.  Known ground: sb-posix has no stat-blksize/stat-blocks
    (project memory), so these two fields have no source today.
  rows 52, 53, 66, 68, 72  `-B`, `!-T`, `at EOF`, `now -B`, `-f() "`: the
    -T/-B text-vs-binary heuristic (perl reads the first block and counts
    odd characters; PCL's answer differs), including its behaviour at EOF.
  row 73  `stat returns full 13 elements` -- got 1, expected 13.  A `stat`
    whose result is compared in a context PCL flattens to a count.
  rows 75, 76, 77  `lstat *_ croaks after stat` / `lstat \*_` / `-l _`:
    perl croaks "The stat preceding lstat() wasn't an lstat"; PCL returns
    ''.  The `_` handle's kind is not remembered.
  rows 90, 91  `-T _ doesn't break the statbuffer` / `... lstat for
    unreadable file`: a filetest on `_` must not disturb the cached buffer.
  row 106  `stat inside stat gets scalar context` -- got '1-2-3--4-5-6'.

Each cluster is independent; the two cheapest are row 73 and row 106 (context),
and the `_`-cache trio is one fact.  The file is now a good measuring
instrument: every row it has is produced.
subject: op/stat.t's 14 rows -- the file runs all 111 of perl's rows for the first time; six clusters (rdev/blocks, -T/-B heuristics, the `_` cache croaks, stat in scalar context)
